name: Panko Chicken Schnitzel with Brown Butter & Capers
author: Thomas Keller

items: 4 skinless, boneless chicken breast halves (about 6 ounces each), butterflied and pounded 1/4-inch-thick

method: Set the flour, eggs, and panko in three separate shallow bowls. Season the chicken cutlets with salt and pepper. Dredge the chicken in the flour, shaking off any excess, then dip in the eggs and coat thoroughly with the panko, pressing lightly to adhere.

In each of 2 large skillets, heat 1/4 cup of canola oil. Add the chicken and cook over moderately high heat, turning once, until golden and crispy, about 3 minutes per side. Transfer the chicken to a paper towel-lined baking sheet and sprinkle with salt, then transfer to plate.

Meanwhile, in a small saucepan, melt the butter and cook over moderately high heat until browned and nutty, about 4 minutes. Stir in the capers, lemon juice, and parsley; spoon over the chicken and serve.

name: Hainanese-Inspired Chicken Rice and Broth
author: Lucy Rosenberg

items: 2 Birds Eye chillies, finely chopped (deseeded if you want)
Splash of neutral oil for frying
2 spring onions, white part, finely chopped
1 bok choy, cooked in the leftover chicken stock

method: Start with the broth, add all the ingredients to a pot, simmer with the lid on.

For the rice, sauté the ginger and spring onion in the neutral oil for 1-2 min before adding in the washed rice & sesame oil. Give a mix then add in the chicken stock. Cook using the absorption method until it's nice and fluffy.
For the chicken, mix together all the ingredients except the chicken breast. Coat the chicken in the marinade.

Fry both sides of the chicken in neutral oil until charred on medium heat. Add in the leftover sauce once chicken is cooked. Cook for a further 1 min. Remove from the pan & cook the bok choy plus the remaining chicken stock in it.
For the chilli lime sauce, heat the neutral oil and carefully pour over the garlic and chilli. Add in the sesame oil, soy sauce & lime juice. Mix.
Assemble. Place rice on the bottom, pour in the broth, chicken & bok choy on top, garnish with spring onions & cucumber. Spoon over the chilli lime sauce.

name: Massaman Curry (Chicken)
author: Naz Deravian
notes: The original method is behind the NYT paywall; these steps are a guide. Don't shake the coconut milk: the thick cream on top is used to fry the paste. Swap the chicken for beef, prawns or tofu if you like.

items: 4 to 6 tablespoons Thai red curry paste, to heat preference
2 (14-ounce) cans full-fat coconut milk (do not shake)
2 large shallots, thinly sliced in rounds
1 pound Yukon gold potatoes (about 2 potatoes), peeled or unpeeled, cut into 1-inch cubes
1½ to 2 pounds boneless skinless chicken thighs, cut into 1-inch pieces
¼ cup dry-roasted, unsalted peanuts, plus more for serving
2 tablespoons fish sauce, plus more as needed
2 teaspoons granulated, light brown or palm sugar, plus more as needed
2 teaspoons Thai tamarind concentrate, or lime juice, plus more as needed

method: Toast the cardamom, coriander seeds, cumin seeds, cinnamon and cloves in a dry pan until fragrant, then grind with the nutmeg and mix into the red curry paste.
Spoon the thick cream from the top of the coconut milk into a pot and fry over medium heat until it starts to split. Add the curry paste and fry for 2-3 minutes until fragrant.
Add the shallots and chicken and stir to coat, then add the rest of the coconut milk, the potatoes and peanuts. Simmer gently for 20-25 minutes until the chicken and potatoes are tender.
Season with fish sauce, sugar and tamarind, tasting and adjusting until salty, sweet and sour are balanced.
Serve with jasmine rice, topped with coriander and extra peanuts.

name: Thai Green Curry
author: Nagi

items: 4 – 6 tbsp Thai Green Curry Paste (Maesri best) OR (Note 1)
1 cup (250ml) chicken or vegetable broth, low sodium
6 kaffir lime leaves, torn in half (Note 5)
350 g/12 oz chicken thigh, skinless boneless, sliced (Note 6)
Crispy fried Asian shallots, high recommended (Note 9)
Green or red chillies slices, optional

method: Heat oil in a heavy based skillet or pot over medium high heat.
Add curry paste (and garlic, ginger and lemongrass extras, if using a jar paste) and cook for 2 to 3 minutes until it mostly "dries out".
Add chicken broth and coconut milk, mix to dissolve paste. Season with 1 tsp fish sauce and 1 tsp sugar for jar paste (3 tsp of each plus 1/8 tsp salt for homemade paste).
Add kaffir lime leaves. Mix then bring to simmer.
Add chicken, stir then lower heat to medium so it's bubbling gently. Cook 7 minutes.
Add eggplants, cook 5 minutes until soft.
Taste sauce. Add fish sauce or salt for more saltiness, sugar for sweetness.
Add snow peas, cook 2 minutes until a bit softened, then stir through basil and lime juice. The sauce should still be on the thin side; don't keep simmering or it will darken.
Serve curry over jasmine rice with garnishes of choice.

name: Pork Mince Stir Fry with Cabbage Slaw
author: Adam Bush
notes: The original method wasn't saved; these steps are a guide.
method: Finely shred the cabbage and toss with half the sesame oil, the rice vinegar and a pinch of sugar. Set aside to lightly pickle.
Grate the ginger and garlic and slice the spring onions, keeping the whites and greens separate.
Heat the remaining sesame oil in a wok over high heat. Add the pork mince and fry, breaking it up, until browned and a little crispy.
Add the ginger, garlic and spring onion whites and cook for a minute. Stir the miso and soy into the water and add to the pan, cooking until saucy.
Serve the pork over rice with the cabbage slaw, sesame seeds and spring onion greens.

name: Tomahawk Steak (Reverse Sear)
author: Nagi Maehashi
notes: Use a meat thermometer. Serve with cowboy butter, béarnaise, mushroom sauce or chimichurri.

items: Cowboy butter (pictured in post – Tomahawk worthy!)
Red wine sauce (page 327 of Dinner, requires homemade beef stock)

method: De-chill - Take the steak out of the fridge 1 hour prior to cooking. Remove from packaging and pat the surface dry. (Do not salt).
Preheat the oven to 140°C/285°F (120°C fan-forced).
Season - Sprinkle the steak meat with salt and pepper, then use your hands to rub it in.
Slow(ish) roast - Put the steak on a rack and set it on a baking tray. Bake for 40 to 45 minutes, or until the internal temperature is 50°C/122°F (for medium rare).
Rest - Take the tray out of the oven and leave the steak on the counter for 10 minutes.
Preheat the BBQ on high until it's screaming hot.
Oil - Drizzle the oil on the steak and lightly pat to spread (don't rub off the salt).
Turn the BBQ down to low or medium-low just before putting the tomahawk on.
Edges first - Using tongs, hold the steak upright and sear the edges and bone first, rotating every minute or so. Watch for flare-ups.
Steak crust - Then place the steak down and cook for 3 to 4 minutes on each side, or until the internal temperature is 55°C / 131°F.
Rest the steak on a rack for 3 minutes - the internal temperature will rise to 57°C/135°F, which is perfect medium rare.
Serve - Cut into 1 cm / 0.4" thick slices and serve with steak sauce of choice.

name: Sausage and Pea Orzo Risotto
author: Kerry Saretsky

items: 10 ounces Italian sausage, removed from its casing
3 cups hot water or low-sodium homemade or store-bought vegetable or chicken stock
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

method: Heat the oil in a medium saucepan over medium-high heat until shimmering. Add the sausage and cook, breaking it up into small pieces until no longer pink.
Add the shallot and sauté until translucent, about 1 minute. Add the orzo and water or stock, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan.

Bring to a boil, then cover, and reduce the heat to medium-low. Cook, stirring occasionally, until the orzo has absorbed all the liquid and is cooked through (add more liquid if the orzo starts to dry out or stick). Season to taste with salt and pepper.
Stir in the peas, and allow to cook for a minute or two just to thaw. Remove from the heat, and stir in the Parmesan and parsley. Serve immediately.

name: Steak au Poivre & Frites
author: Laura Sharrad

items: 1 tbs freshly cracked Sarawak or black peppercorns

method: Frites: cut the potatoes into thin chips, dry them extremely well and toss with plenty of olive oil and sea salt flakes. Spread on a lined tray, not touching, and bake at 200°C for about 30 minutes until super golden and crispy.
Season the steak with lots of sea salt flakes and freshly ground pepper.

Place half the butter in a pan over high heat, and when it begins to foam, sear the fillets on each side to gain a crust and cook 3/4 of the way through. Remove from the pan and rest. Don't clean the pan out.
Add the rest of the butter and the cracked peppercorns and fry off.
Deglaze with the Cognac, and flambé the contents of the pan if you're confident, or reduce by half.
Pour the cream into the pan and allow to bubble lightly, add the steak back in and finish cooking gently.
Pour the sauce over the steak and serve with hot frites.

name: Ribeye Steak
author: Ali Slagle
notes: The original method is behind the NYT paywall; these steps are a guide. Good with a rocket salad, green beans or potatoes.

items: 2 (12- to 16-ounce) boneless ribeye steaks, at least 1-inch thick, patted dry

method: Pat the steaks dry and season generously with salt and pepper. Leave at room temperature for 30 minutes if you can.
Heat the oil in a cast-iron skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering. Add the steaks and cook, flipping every minute or so, until well browned, 8-10 minutes for medium-rare (52°C inside).
Turn the heat to low, add the butter, shallot and herbs, and baste the steaks with the foaming butter for a minute or two.
Rest the steaks for 5-10 minutes, then slice and spoon over the pan butter.

name: Pasta alla Zozzona
author: On Trac 5

items: 1 tbsp Italian Style Chilli oil or olive oil
60g finely grated Pecorino Romano cheese, plus more for serving
Salt and freshly ground black pepper
150g hot Italian sausage, removed from casing

method: Cook rigatoni per the packet directions.
In a small bowl, beat the egg yolks and Pecorino cheese together with a fork until a thick paste forms. Season with a few grindings of black pepper and stir in 1/4 cup of pasta water. Set aside.
Drizzle the oil into a large pan. Add the sausage and use a wooden spoon to break it into pieces as it cooks.
Add the guanciale to the pan. Once it turns golden and crispy, add the onion and garlic.
When the onion becomes translucent, add the passata. Stir gently and cook on medium-low heat for 15 minutes.
Sprinkle fresh basil into the sauce and stir gently. Then, add the cooked pasta together with the egg yolk and Pecorino cheese mixture.
Stir and toss until the pasta is well coated. Finish by adding more Pecorino cheese and black pepper.
